GTA 6 NPCs Could Be The Biggest Thing In Gaming Yet

Details
by Obaid ur Rehman
on September 20, 2026
Grand Theft Auto VI
Twitter Facebook Reddit Copy Link
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 6:04
Instaread

NPCs have become an increasingly important part of modern open-world games, helping make their worlds feel more alive and reactive. Rockstar Games has already pushed this idea forward with Red Dead Redemption 2, where characters can react to your actions, comment on what you do, and respond differently depending on their personalities.

Greet and antagonize interactions are a good example of this. Rather than simply serving as background characters, NPCs in RDR2 can acknowledge the player's presence and react to the situations around them. However, everything we have seen so far suggests that GTA 6 is taking this idea much further.

From NPC-driven events and spontaneous crimes to social media activity and characters reacting to Jason and Lucia in different ways, the people inhabiting Leonida could become a much more active part of the world. If Rockstar delivers on what it has shown so far, GTA 6 could set a new benchmark for NPCs in open-world games.

NPCs In GTA 6 Aren't Just Decorations

People have understandably focused on the graphics, Lucia and Jason, and the overall visual fidelity shown in the game's extended view. Those are the elements that immediately stand out. However, the previews and everything we have learned so far also point towards just how ambitious the world simulation in GTA 6 could be.

In many games, NPCs primarily exist to populate the world. Games such as Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 and RDR2 have already pushed beyond that, with characters following routines, reacting to the player, interacting with their surroundings, and responding to different situations. Even then, much of what they do remains tied to their individual routines or scripted interactions.

GTA 6 appears to be taking another step forward by making these characters a more active part of the world itself. They are not simply being placed around Vice City and the surrounding areas to make them look populated. Instead, they can seemingly influence and participate in what is happening around them.

There are going to be NPC-driven events, different reactions to Jason and Lucia, the return of greet and antagonize interactions, characters participating in robberies, NPCs intervening when you are committing a crime, events that can happen without any input from the player, social media activity generated by the world, greater variation in character models and animations, and behavior that can apparently continue independently of what the player is doing.

The return of greet and antagonize is particularly interesting. The basic idea remains similar to what we saw in RDR2, so the interaction itself may not be radically different. The bigger change could come from how characters respond based on their personalities, the situation they are in, and their relationship with Jason or Lucia.

NPCs Can Become Part Of Your Crimes

One of the biggest changes is that NPCs can potentially become directly involved in your crimes.

In GTA 5, you could walk into a store, pull out a weapon, rob the cashier, and leave while preparing for the police response. The interaction was largely between you and the store employee, with law enforcement becoming involved after the crime was reported. In GTA 6, however, another person could potentially step in if they believe they have an opportunity to stop you.

NPCs can also seemingly create their own situations without the player being directly involved. World events and robberies can take place without you triggering them, which could fundamentally change how random encounters work in GTA.

Think about how random events generally worked in GTA 5. You would enter a trigger area, the activity would begin, and you could then decide whether to get involved or simply drive away.

In GTA 6, that relationship appears to be changing. Instead of always being the reason an event begins, you could simply come across something that was already happening in the world.

Imagine driving around Leonida and coming across two people arguing, a robbery in progress, someone being chased, a traffic incident, a fight, an accident, an NPC fleeing, police responding to a situation, people recording an incident, or a group gathering somewhere.

The important distinction is that you may not be responsible for any of it. You could simply happen to be in the right place at the right time, or perhaps the wrong place at the wrong time.

The Social Media System Could Make NPCs Even More Important

GTA 6's social network could add another layer to this dynamic world. Characters can post content online, meaning that events taking place around Leonida could potentially become part of the game's social media ecosystem.

Imagine an NPC doing something unusual, another character witnessing it, someone recording the moment, and that footage eventually appearing online. You could then discover the post yourself and decide to travel to the location where it happened.

This creates a pretty interesting loop:

  • The world creates an event.
  • NPCs react to it.
  • Someone records what happened.
  • The footage appears on social media.
  • The player discovers it.
  • The player can then travel to the location and investigate for themselves.

This is one of the areas where the world simulation and social media system could work particularly well together. Instead of the game simply presenting information to you, the world itself could become the source of that information.

These characters are not simply walking around to make Vice City look busy. They could interact with each other, create events, react to the player, commit crimes, respond to crimes, record incidents, post about them online, and generally contribute to what is happening around them.

If GTA 6 manages to achieve all of this at the scale Rockstar appears to be aiming for, its approach to NPCs could become one of the biggest advancements in open-world gaming yet.

What are your thoughts on the NPCs in GTA 6? Please share your thoughts with us in the comments section below. For more information on the game, check out our GTA 6 section for additional details on Rockstar Games' upcoming Grand Theft Auto entry.
